result:
`final.py` scores **0.5592** on the search split, up from the LRU baseline's 0.365. I used **18 of the 24 scorer calls**. One of those, an early hill-climbing version, came back invalid because of a bug that evicted the key being requested; I fixed it before going on.

**What final.py does:** it's a W-TinyLFU cache: a small recency window in front of a main area, and a newcomer gets into the main area only if it has been requested more often than the entry it would push out. It also runs 16 cheap "shadow" copies of the cache side by side, combining 4 window sizes (1%, 5%, 20%, 90% of capacity) with 4 lengths of request-count memory (counts halve every 4×, 10×, 30× or 100× capacity requests). Every `capacity` requests the real cache switches to the settings of whichever shadow has had the best recent hit rate. It only switches when that shadow is clearly ahead, so it doesn't flip back and forth on noise.

**Search-split hit rate by trace:**

| trace | LRU-style (ARC) | fixed W-TinyLFU | final |
|---|---|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.240 | 0.240 | 0.244 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.299 | 0.644 | 0.659 |
| phases | 0.635 | 0.635 | 0.633 |
| mixed | 0.261 | 0.267 | 0.277 |
| recency | 0.847 | 0.716 | 0.846 |
| shifting_loops | 0.164 | 0.698 | 0.697 |

The baseline score didn't come with per-trace numbers, so the first column is ARC (overall 0.407), a policy that adapts between recency and frequency.

**How it got there:**
- **The big jump** (0.41 → 0.53) came from frequency-based admission, which handles loops larger than the cache far better than recency-based policies. That alone dropped "recency" to 0.716.
- **Choosing the window size with shadow caches** (0.553) recovered "recency" without hurting the loop traces. Two other ways of adapting the window size did worse: a gradual hill climb, and resizing based on recently evicted keys.
- **Shadows with different count-memory lengths** (0.558) mostly helped mixed and loop_and_hot.
- **Shrinking the main area's protected part from 80% to 30%** (0.559) gave a large gain on my own synthetic loop traces but only about +0.001 on the real ones.
- **Tried and dropped:** evicting the least-frequent of several old entries, counters capped at 15, and an even longer count memory (never chosen).

**Caveats:**
- **Plateau:** the last several changes moved the score by only about 0.001, so I stopped rather than spend the remaining 6 calls tuning to the search traces.
- **Speed:** it does about 17× the work of LRU. Locally it took about 2.5 s per 320k requests and about 5 s on a 600k-request stress test, run at the lowest priority on a busy machine. Every real scorer run finished inside the 8 s limit, but the margin would get thin if the unseen traces are much longer.
- **Local benchmark:** my synthetic traces predicted the real scorer poorly, so the decisions above rest on real scorer results.

Files are in `eval/loop-bench/runs/r29/u4/cache/`:
- `final.py`
- `work/` (all candidates and my local test scripts)
